DRIVER EDUCATION & SAFETY AT A GLANCE 
Statutes: Chapter 1001, Education Code 
Rules: Title 16 T.A.C. Chapter 84 
Practice Act? Yes 
Title Act? Yes 
Inspections? Yes 
Facilities? Yes 
Individuals? Yes

Overview: 
Anyone between the ages of 14 and 25 who wants to apply for a driver 
license in Texas must complete a driver education course before 
receiving a license. Students have three options for completing a driver 
education course: 
● Enrolling in a driver education school 
● Enrolling in a parent taught course 
● Completing driver education at a public school, education service 
center, college, or university. 
TDLR maintains a list of driver education providers:  Driver Education 
Provider Search (texas.gov). 
Instruction 
The classroom phase of a driver education course is at least 24 hours. 
The in-car phase consists of 7 hours of behind-the-wheel driving, 7 hours 
of in-car observation, and an additional 30 hours of behind-the-wheel 
driving (10 of these hours must be done at night). The additional 30 hours 
of behind-the-wheel driving is monitored by the parent or guardian and 
is not required to be provided by a licensed driver education provider. 
However, the hours must be completed in the presence of an adult 
who holds a valid license, is 21 or older, has at least one year of driving 
experience, and occupies the seat next to the driver. 
● To obtain a Learner License, a student must be 15 years of age 
or older; have completed the first 6 hours of driver education or 
all 24 hours of classroom instruction; and have received a Texas 
driver education certificate of completion (DE-964). 
● To obtain a Provisional License, a student must have held the 
learner license for at least 6 months, be 16 years old or older, 
have completed all driver education hours (24 classroom and 44 
in-car hours) and pass the driving exam. Once the driving exam is 
successfully completed, the Texas Department of Public Safety will 
issue a driver license. 
Curriculum 
Driver Education & Safety Providers must use Texas Education Code 
1001, 16 Texas Administrative Code, Chapter 84, and the program guides 
when teaching a driver education & safety course. 
During a legislative session, there may be mandates that require 
changes to the Driver Education & Safety curriculum.  Each Driver 
Education & Safety Provider is required to make these necessary 
changes in order to be in compliance and meet the obligations as a 
TDLR licensed Driver Education & Safety Provider. 
TDLR also oversees Driving Safety courses. 
Driving safety courses  must encourage the observance of traffic laws 
and try to reduce the number of traffic violations and traffic-related 
injuries, deaths, and economic losses. Classes must be at least 6 hours 
long if they are to be used for traffic citation dismissal. The court must 
approve taking a driving safety course to dismiss a citation. A driving 
safety course must cost at least $25.00. 
License Required to Operate School or Teach 
A person may not operate a school or course unless the person holds a 
Driver Training Provider license. A person may not teach a driver education 
course unless the person holds a driver education instructor license.    
Driver Education Instructor license: TAC 84.44 
● hold a valid class A, B, C, or CDL driver’s license, other than a 
learner license or provisional license, for the preceding three years, 
that has not been revoked or suspended in the preceding three 
years; 
● submit a national criminal history record information review fee; 
and 
● provide fingerprints to the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) 
through the IdentoGo Fingerprint Service or any other method 
required by the DPS. 
● A license fee of $50.00 
Driver Education Provider license 
● $10,000.00 driver education bond 
● Assumed Name Registration document from the Texas Secretary of 
States office 
● Registered Agent – If business is located outside of Texas 
● $500.00 application fee 
● $300.00 endorsement fee (online, in-person, parent taught) 
● Driver education curriculum that includes the required topics in 
the program of organized instruction, and requirements in Texas 
Administrative Code Chapter 84, Texas Education Code 1001

A driver education instructor shall carry their 
instructor license at all times while instructing 
a driver education course. 
The Driver Training and Traffic Safety 
Advisory Board has 9 members serving 
staggered 6-year terms, which includes: 
● Three driver education providers 
● Three driving safety providers 
● One driver education instructor 
● One representative of the Department of 
Public Safety 
● One public member
